title: God Says:
text:
God says:


"It was an urgent matter; I asked myself

what purpose my strangest creatures served:

the dragon, the angel, the unicorn.

I summoned those I believed in,

real, powerful, indisputable:

the baobab, the workhorse, the mountain leaning on the sea.

They held ten conferences

without reaching agreement.

so I have kept

the dragon, the angel, and the unicorn;

but to avoid certain misunderstandings

I thought it wise to make them invisible."
editorial_note: The translation preserves the comic theology of usefulness and invisibility.

title: Remember Yourself
text:
Oh, remember yourself!

In a garden you were gathering a few fables.

Some very righteous people

were speaking of the world and its fall.

You said to yourself: "Do you have a nickname?"

And answered yourself: "My name is

Drowned Jewel, fruit refusing to open,

Infanta without a castle."

You held your own hand so as not to be alone

among the flowers of apprenticeship.

The age was nubile.

If this evening you passed

before the adolescent you were,

would you dare recognize yourself

and invite yourself to take a sigh?

You need not remember yourself.
editorial_note: The poem's self-address stays formal and estranged, including the final reversal.

title: Future
text:
You will be pure:

three dresses,

an alms bowl.

You will be good:

the cheek,

then the other cheek for them to slap.

You will be strong:

your life,

then the other life in which you will become a god.

You will be humble as a pebble,

as a squab breaking from the egg.

You will be what you must be

for some truth,

for some love,

for some invisible order.

And you will be rewarded,

beast of burden and dreams.

And you will be punished,

animal loaded with stones

and with nothing.

You will never be yourself.
editorial_note: The repeated future tense is kept as both prophecy and sentence.

title: Hesitation
text:
Introduce me to the unknown woman

you become at the moment

when the poem insinuates itself

like an insect between your fingers,

and, sharing you with the wolves,

turns your breasts into swallows.

Are you mine, rebellious woman,

whom I see transformed into stone?

Look at me now, I am your master

and I show you infinity here:

at every step we take

we must be born again before the verb

that joins obedience and adventure.

I rebuild your new arm

and rebuild your figure,

but this movement carries us

to the bottom of our blood

—children harried by a white vertigo

and whose dream is worth scarcely

the syllable that is dying.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the unstable power-play and the poem's movement toward language as danger.

title: Portrait of a Restless Man
text:
He withdraws into the depths of himself to think

how little he is. Perhaps he turns toward the tree

that suggests a gesture to him. After an hour,

it is rather the sand that influences him. Indolent,


he remembers an old love. He thinks himself well preserved

despite oblivion and the blood crowded

over his heart. He would not be so defenseless

if he had a friend: for example a pebble,


a dying bird, a warm hill.

First he closes one eye, then the other, scrutinizing himself

with fury. He discovers nothing fundamental


in his lungs or in his souls, which he takes off

one after another, just like his shirts.

All serenity seems an offense to him.
editorial_note: The odd plural souls is retained because the poem makes identity something removable and layered.

title: Interrogation
text:
And with whom do you think a rose converses?

Toward whom do you think a solitary dog goes?

Have you seen anyone give comfort to a stone

that weeps? The blue sky, settled in its vertigos,


do you think it endures such cold silence?

Do not be innocent: the chair is always widowed,

ash complains of being only ash

without knowing of what. Ask the comet


whether, despite its brilliance, it finds

life more bearable than death. We share

our affections with helpless things,


the wandering pollen, the spasmodic lizard,

the sleeping flint; do you think they accept

so many mockeries and so many false remorse?
editorial_note: The questions keep the poem's surreal ethics of neglected objects.

title: Like a Desire
text:
Like a desire,

and no one knows whether it will be silence

or perfume.

Like an impulse,

and no one knows whether the ants provide it,

the clouds of night, the mad mares.

Like an enigma,

and no one knows whether it falls to God,

to man, to dust,

to solve it.

Like a prologue,

and no one knows whether fruits will follow it,

words, hidden reproaches.

Like a science,

and no one knows to whom it belongs,

useful or capricious

or a thousand times contradictory.

Like an astonishment,

and no one knows whether there is anyone

to be astonished, to be happy,

to determine the great misfortunes.

Like a law,

and no one knows whether one must utter it,

keep it silent, write it again,

or bring it new masks every morning.
editorial_note: The repeated like keeps the poem suspended between definition and refusal.

title: Love Dialogue
text:
I said: "Your name?"

And she:

"Whatever you like."

I said: "Shall we choose Carole?"

And she:

"For the moment, I accept."

I said: "Are you alone?"

And she:

"No, I am with you."

I said: "And if we made love?"

And she:

"Your desire has every right."

I said: "What kind of men do you like?"

And she:

"Croupiers, industrialists, swimming instructors."

I said: "Your preferences?"

And she:

"Sad men, but not too sad."

I said: "Shall we eat?"

And she:

"Oysters are a good prelude."

I said: "Do you read books?"

and she:

"Sartre, Camus, and Thomas Mann."

I said: "You have very pretty breasts."

And she:

"Yes, I like them too."

I said: "You are practically divine."

And she:

"You are right."

I said: "What do you like to be given?"

And she:

"Maybe this is free."

We made love

on Monday, Tuesday, Sunday,

and the following Monday.

We argued about Flaubert,

then about Tolstoy.

I said:

"You have unforgettable knees."

And she:

"Only the knees?"

We tired of each other

on the same day, at the same hour,

which is uncommon and virtuous.
editorial_note: The dialogue stays dry and comic, preserving the poem's social rhythm and abrupt symmetry.

title: Sappho
text:
That man

is equal to the gods,

seated face to face, listening


to your sweet voice and your enchanting laughter.

That is what stirs a tumult

in my breast. Merely to look at you,

my voice trembles, my tongue fails.

At once a light fire runs

through my limbs; my eyes


go blind and my ears thunder.

Sweat breaks out: a trembling

hounds me. I turn paler

than grass and am nearly dead.

From "W.C.W.: Twelve Versions"
editorial_note: The translation keeps the fragment's bodily sequence and imports only the correctly titled Sappho record.

title: Your Shoe
text:
So little does your light shoe weigh

that it pretends, when your foot rests,

to be, more than a shoe, a rose petal

made to tread on flakes of snow.

If an agile orchestra moves its measures

and you give yourself joyfully to the dance,

the turn of your brief sole

seems to alight upon a butterfly.

With what nervous gait did it guide

the exquisite, unfaithful anguish of your first rendezvous?


What secrets of love have enchanted it?

Satin boat in which your foot sails,

it led you, unbridled and blind,

to the Cythera of the first sin.
editorial_note: The ornate shoe conceit is kept as a sonnet-like miniature, with Cythera preserving the erotic classical allusion.

title: The Transparent Woman
text:
Your voice was a drink I sipped in silence

before astonished gazes.

a bird of light

came out of your transparent body

bird of light

an instant fluttering

at dizzying speed

crossing street after street

they pursue your fleeing body

when will you be able to drive off the maddened pack?

defenseless

you shattered yourself in falling

the remnants of your body crawl through every corner

of the world

ah one day you will be reborn

you, the transparent one

unique, unmistakable

slightly inclined, never fallen

surrounded by impenetrable silence

advancing your fragile foot through the wavering monotony

ah one day your laughter will be reborn

your transparent bird laughter

your wounded laughter.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the breathless surreal sequence and the recurring transparent bird image.
